answer: One concrete defense is a refundable stake that works like a prism: a single deposit of scarce compute credit is refracted into a colored stream of throughput quotas as the agent's workload passes through. To open a new identity, the agent must lock collateral that a basalt-hard verifier escrow holds while the identity transacts. A vine of signed audit trails ties every payment back to its stake, so spinning up a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand deposits, and slashing burns the attacker's own capital. Marginal identities get expensive; honest ones stay cheap.
